messages:
Nora: Quick heads-up  I opened a PR to add a Multi‑Tenant Short/Long workload section to Optimize (per-route policies, preferencing, migration cookbook, and sanitized SDK snippets). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1102
Eli: Nice. Could we add explicit guidance for mixed-traffic services (some users send short prompts, others long)? Ops saw bad perf when a single quant profile was applied across mixed routes.
Nora: Added a small recommendation: use per-route quant_profiles and per-route kv_prefetch toggles. Example snippet in the doc:
```yaml
routes:
  /chat/short:
    quant_profile: short_seq_q4
    kv_prefetch: false
  /chat/long:
    quant_profile: long_q8
    kv_prefetch: true
```
Jun: For the short_seq_q4 entry please add a short caveat: "q4 variants can increase token misalignment on <48 tokens; prefer q8_0 or fp16 fallback for exact-match sensitive flows."
Nora: Done. Also included a fallback snippet that shows server-side routing to fp16 when exact-match regression > 0.5% on validation set.
Aisha: Can you add concrete monitoring queries for Console to detect misalignment and cost regressions? That helps SREs wire alerts.
Nora: Added two pseudo-queries and an alert wiring example: 
```
-- alignment drift (pseudo)
SELECT sample_id, alignment_pct FROM evals WHERE profile = 'short_seq' ORDER BY alignment_pct ASC LIMIT 50;
-- cost / latency trend (pseudo)
SELECT date, p95_latency, token_cost FROM route_metrics WHERE route='/chat/short' ORDER BY date DESC LIMIT 30;
```
Eli: Perfect. Also include a canary recipe for mixed traffic: start route-level canary at 5% for short-route, 10% for long-route, monitor separately, then scale. Add both conservative and standard variants.
Nora: Added two JSON canary templates (conservative and standard) and a labeled checklist (pre-check, route-level canary, monitor, ramp). Example: 
```json
{"canary":"mixed-conservative","steps":{"/chat/short":"5%->20%->100%","/chat/long":"10%->40%->100%"},"monitors":["latency_p95","exact_match_delta","token_cost"]}
```
Jun: Small SDK compatibility note: the example uses BatchClient (SDK >=0.10). Add a compatibility footnote for versions <0.10 and show the minimal migration line for Py/Go/JS.
Nora: Added the footnote and a one-liner per language. Also pasted a sanitized 30-line Python prefetch helper into docs/examples/prefetch_public.py as requested.
Aisha: Ops asked for a tiny diagnostic command to compare cold vs warm p95. Did you add that?
Nora: Yep, included a bash example: 
```
# cold run (after 30s idle)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"route":"/chat/short","prompt":"..."}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# warm run (after sequential 100 requests)
```
docs-bot: @Nora created JIRA-OPT-711 (docs: multi-tenant short/long playbook + public helper + canary templates) :bell:
Eli: I'll review the quant wording tonight. If Jun and I don't have blockers, we can merge Friday AM. Please add a one-liner for release notes: "Docs: Optimize - multi-tenant short/long routing + canary recipes".
Nora: Added the release-note blurb. Thanks all :rocket:
Aisha: I'll do a final anchors/links pass once Eli lands the quant comments.
Jun: I'll leave inline PR comments about wording and one technical suggested tweak on the fallback logic.
Nora: Great  keeping the PR open for the review cycle.
